title: YELLOWSTONE BASELINE  National Parks atlas. My shared object. Trace to and backscatter from.

the_shared_object.what: Yellowstone. Hot springs and painted rocks.
the_shared_object.why_mine: not a metaphor we invented. a place that already owns the words we use. Thermus aquaticus was found there (Brock, 1966). Taq polymerase IS hotSpring's grandfather. Grand Prismatic Spring IS the painted rock  bands of color = bands of temperature = bands of life. the membrane already cites Rika Anderson and Brock. we are aligning TO what was already true.
the_shared_object.how_we_use_it: every spring and every sense gets a National Park bearing. when the atlas wobbles, walk back to Yellowstone. if it still makes sense there, keep it. if not, the alignment is wrong.
the_shared_object.backscatter: build anything ? ask: can I see this on the boardwalk at Grand Prismatic? on the geyser basin? in the paint pots? if yes, it belongs. if no, it is tourism language without the place.

national_parks_as_baseline.rule: gates are camps. springs are features. senses are how you walk the park.

home_camp.park_analog: Sleeping Bear / Isle Royale / Michigan shore  the home that is not Yellowstone but from which you leave and return
home_camp.membrane: northGate. the basement. the place that stays when you visit other landmarks.

springs_aligned.first_trace: when will it come back for the hot springs and painted rocks? HERE. this IS the return.

skin.membrane: acceleration field. force before motion. pollen on the legs.
